links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 14, Excel Spreadsheets
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: reading and writing workbooks, the two projects, fonts, formulas, sizes, merging, freezing and charts.

links.title: openpyxl - A Python library to read/write Excel 2010 xlsx/xlsm files
links.why: The library's home page, with its sample code and its security note about XML attacks and defusedxml.

links.title: Tutorial - openpyxl documentation
links.why: Workbooks, worksheets, cell access, iter_rows and values_only, saving and the flags of load_workbook such as data_only and read_only.

links.title: Optimised Modes - openpyxl documentation
links.why: Read-only and write-only workbooks for very large files, and what each of them cannot do.

links.title: Parsing Formulas - openpyxl documentation
links.why: The Tokenizer that splits a formula into tokens and the Translator that moves a formula to another cell.

links.title: Dates and Times - openpyxl documentation
links.why: How dates are stored as numbers, the 1900 and 1904 date systems, the leap-year error and why no timezone can be stored.

links.title: Charts - openpyxl documentation
links.why: The chart types, the steps of creating a chart and its default size and anchor.

links.title: zipfile - Work with ZIP archives
links.why: The standard-library module that opens the zip archive an .xlsx file is, which the page's playground program uses to write and read a workbook.

links.title: xml.etree.ElementTree - The ElementTree XML API
links.why: Parsing the XML parts of a workbook with the standard library, as the playground program does.

links.title: pprint - Data pretty printer
links.why: pformat, which writes Project 9's dictionary as Python source, and its sort_dicts parameter.

_note: Every url was opened with a page fetch (curl through the session proxy) and its content read on the date in 'checked'; titles are those of the pages, without the site name. The openpyxl pages on that date were headed version 3.1.3 and the Python documentation pages 3.14.8, while the chapter research executed openpyxl 3.1.5 under Python 3.14.4. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read, so the page offers labelled searches instead and the course owner may add checked ones here.
